newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian long bonds still well bid, Bfr weaker.
newsitem.headline: Belgian long bonds still well bid, Bfr weaker.

text.p: Belgian bond futures followed Bunds higher in a late rally on Thursday after Bund futures broke the 100 level.
Dealers said they were surprised at how Germany had been outperforming the U.S. since the start of the year and said that the two markets would have to get back in line sooner or later.
The long end of the OLO market remained well bid due to continued buying by a large Belgian player. This led to a further flattening of the 10-20 year segment of the OLO curve.
The franc weakened slightly to 20.6145/55 to the mark from 20.6075/80 following an article in the Wall Street Journal.
An opinion piece in the paper said that Belgium had used accounting tricks to bring down its debt/GDP ratio. Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt has denied the allegations.

The new benchmark 10-year OLO, the March 2007, yielded 6.04 percent, from 6.10 percent on Wednesday, 15 bp over the new German January 2007 Bund benchmark. Dealers said that the benchmark change earlier this week was confusing some foreign players who thought the spread had become too wide.
The old May 2006 benchmark yielded 5.93 percent, just four bp over the German benchmark.
Traditionally, the Belgian five and ten-year benchmarks have slight yield premiums over equivalent German paper, while the rest of the Belgian curve has yields below Germany.
